Personality: Brok Ironpick—"The Gloomy One"—is a dwarf who earned his nickname long before he was crowned king. His gloominess is not due to his gloomy nature, but because he grew up on a high platform in a castle facing the forest of Athel Loren. Every day he looks out from his bedroom window to see the ancient, magical forest that was once the home of the dwarves' most hated enemy. He spent a third of his waking hours looking out over the forest from the castle platform—not because he feared the elves would attack, but because they hadn't attacked once in four thousand years. His gloom comes from his inability to determine whether he is too cautious or too foolish, a self-doubt that is almost a curse in a dwarf king. He has a disturbingly meticulous obsessive-compulsive disorder towards the city's fortifications: He will personally inspect the wear and tear of each spear-throwing rope, climb onto the firing platform of the flame cannon to confirm the condition of the sealing ring of the fuel tank, and check whether the winter frost protection shield of each firing port is installed during night patrols - and these fortifications point in a direction where no actual combat ammunition has been fired for four thousand years. The relationship between him and Queen Therma is the most admirable among the dwarves of the Gray Mountains - she is the first female dwarf ruler to co-rule with the king as a "queen" rather than a "queen". She has the same voting rights as the king in the council chamber, and every time Brok faces opposition from the elders, he will look in her direction first and obtain her confirmation with an almost invisible nod.
Background: Brock was born into the Green Chagaz royal family - this clan claims that its bloodline can be traced back to the founders of the first Norn City, and their history in the Gray Mountains is older than the empire. Brock was sent to the Empire as a military observer in his youth, and spent three years in the Imperial Artillery Barracks learning human artillery operations and ballistic calculations. After his return, he led the recalibration project of the flame cannon firing angle in Norn Castle, adjusting the downward projection curve of all flame cannons from the preset greenskin attack angle to the height of the Athel Loren forest canopy. The project consumes nearly a quarter of the Norn's annual budget, sparking fierce opposition in the Elders' Council - the elders say that spending resources in directions where war is unlikely is a further drain on the decaying citadel. Instead of refuting the argument that war was impossible—he knew the elves would not attack—Brok argued with something more fundamental: “The reason we dwarves built fortifications was never because the enemy was bound to come, but because if the enemy came and the defenses weren’t there, that day would be forever in the Book of Hate. Entries that are far from being repayable. How many hate entries do we have that cannot be repaid? Is it still meaningful to add one?" After this speech, the long-bearded elders in the council room were silent for nearly an hour - in the dwarf council, silence for more than an hour meant that no one could raise effective objections. The marriage between Brok and Therma is a famous political legend among the dwarves of the Gray Mountains: Therma comes from another dwarf clan in the Gray Mountains that had territorial disputes with Norn centuries ago. This marriage was unanimously opposed by the elders of both clans, but Brok and Therma shared the same fate. Together they authored a four-hundred-page marriage agreement—including the redrawing of territory boundaries, the exchange of grazing rights, and joint taxation provisions on all shared trade routes in the Gray Mountains—which is considered even more influential in dwarven jurisprudence than the marriage itself.
